decisions.quote: The association of the FTO polymorphism (rs8044769) with BMI was not replicated in the Chinese Han population either. The previous studies showed that FTO was associated with BMI [6–12], and two of them referred to rs8044769 as BMI-associated SNP [11, 12]. In the association analysis of rs8044769 with BMI, we found no association between rs8044769 and BMI. And the BMIs corresponding different genotypes of rs8044769 showed no significant difference.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. Dai et al. (2018) empirically evaluate the association between FTO SNP rs8044769 and BMI in their Chinese Han sample (Tables 4 and 5) and explicitly state in the Discussion that the rs8044769–BMI association reported specifically in References 11 and 12 was not replicated. Reference 11 is Zhao et al. (2009, Obesity, 10.1038/oby.2009.159), which is an independent original study absent from shipped row 1152 (Zeggini et al., 2012) and distinct from sibling targets 1, 3, and 4.

decisions.quote: A study on Chinese Han population denied this association, but the subject number of the Chinese study was a little bit small [16]. Until now, the association between FTO and OA remains debatable.Therefore, we evaluated the potential association of the FTO polymorphism (rs8044769) with OA in the Chinese Han population with more cases and controls.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. Dai et al. (2018) explicitly motivate their larger Chinese Han case-control study by noting that the prior Chinese Han study (Reference 16: Wang et al., 2016, Bone Joint Res, 10.1302/2046-3758.55.2000589) denied the rs8044769–OA association in a small sample, re-test the rs8044769–OA and rs8044769–BMI relationships in an enlarged Chinese Han cohort (890 cases and 844 controls), and confirm consistency with Wang et al. (2016) alongside a pooled analysis. Wang et al. (2016) is an independent published study absent from shipped row 1152 (Zeggini et al., 2012) and distinct from sibling targets 1–3.
